A Canadian Morning – Can Canada Liberate the US From the DEA?

All of the stories in this morning’s postings are from Canada, but they are also about qualities that those of us in DEAland do not usually associate with our quiet and quite civilized Northern neighbor – defiance.

Shortly after I started doing this site late last year, it became apparent that Canada was going to be a major source of marijuana news. Of course, I knew about what was going on in Vancouver. Hillary Black of the Vancouver Compassion Club is a good friend and an absolute delight. I have met and become friends with a number of Canadian academics over the years and Marc Emery’s fame extends far beyond Canada.

However, it has been the bravery of Canadian activists and the persistence of Canadian hemp promoters that has put Canada on the front line in the struggle against marijuana prohibition. Then the Olympic Committee did us the great favor of making absolute fools of themselves, as prohibitionists are wont to do.

The fact that the Canadian Health Minister wore a hemp shirt to announce the lifting of the 60 year ban on hemp cultivation highlights a major difference with his counterparts to the south. Can you imagine HHS Secretary wearing a hemp dress? Now there is something that could set hemp fashions back a decade!

While the Canadian government must be under tremendous pressure form DEAland, the Canadians are very experienced at dealing with pressure from their large neighbor. Indeed, that is a lot of what being Canadian is all about. Happily, tweaking superpower noses is an old Canadian sport.

One of these stories, however, is about the looming confrontation between Canada and DEAland over the harassment of Canadian citizens who regularly visit here. A law that was designed to harass Mexicans and other swarthy outlanders is now being used against white folks. This has always gotten the prohibitionists into big trouble in the past. (Not that there is anything racist about marijuana prohibition!) If the Republicans pass a more draconian anti-smuggling law as proposed by Gingrich, et al., a Ross Rebagliati clone is going to be sentenced to life in prison. Then things will get nasty.

In the meantime, it is clear that the Canadians, who have only recently gotten a Constitution, take theirs more seriously than our courts take our tattered remnant. Canada is not going to be able to sustain its suppression of medical cannabis much longer. DEAland opposition may actually make it politically easier for them to make the change.

Vancouver has already opted out of much of marijuana prohibition. Other cities cannot be far behind. The Quebecois are demanding a resolution of the medical marijuana issue. The Canadian newspapers – unlike most of their DEAland counterparts – actually report on what is going on. Marijuana prohibition cannot survive the light of day.

For decades the DEA and its fronts have lied to the American people about the success of the Dutch experience in separating marijuana from hard drugs. It is simply not going to be possible to keep the Canadian experience a secret, although the American media will do their best.

Again, the Internet keeps widening the hole in the curtain of lies that have kept the American people in fear and ignorance. Just as communism could not survive modern communications marijuana prohibition cannot survive the Internet reporting what is going on in Canada and the rest of the world.

One last note: Most Americans have forgotten that Canada exists because it did not choose to join in the American Revolution, and even became a haven for the Tories, who opposed our Founding Fathers. It is hard to imagine the absolute horror and disgust with which the hemp growers and merchants who founded this country must view the terrible irony that the home of the Tories is now the best hope for liberating the country they founded!

Stay tuned, eh.

Richard Cowan
